source.title: How do Cross-View and Cross-Modal Alignment Affect Representations in Contrastive Learning?
source.authors: Thomas M. Hehn; Julian F. P. Kooij; Dariu M. Gavrila

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study investigates how contrastive cross-view and cross-modal training affects visual information in representations, but it does not test whether representations from independently trained models become more similar with scale or test any listed version of that claim.
record.gate_note: The study trains Pri3D variants using VIEW and GEO alignment losses and reports what information their visual representations retain. It does not measure similarity between independently trained models, scaling, or any of the other listed versions. Downstream task scores are not recorded as claim-version findings because they measure task performance, not the claimed convergence.
record.test_reason: The study trains Pri3D variants (VIEW, GEO, combined) on images and point clouds and probes what visual information each retains via frozen/finetuned downstream tasks. It never measures similarity between independently trained models, across scale, seeds or modalities of the claim's kind (image-caption), nor maps one model's representations onto another's. Cross-modal alignment here is a training objective imposed on purpose, not convergence arising independently.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Authors conclude cross-modal alignment discards complementary information (color, texture) and emphasizes redundant depth cues, improving depth prediction, and that GEO pretraining gives the most robust encoders across finetuning tasks and datasets, akin to shape- vs texture-bias findings; frozen-task performance does not predict finetuning performance.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses Pri3D-style VIEW and GEO contrastive training to examine retained visual information; it does not implement or compare the claim's proposed inter-model similarity measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that separating the VIEW and GEO feature spaces with a linear layer changes frozen-task results. Supplementary material also says the pretraining learning rate affects results within versus across datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: Contrastive cross-modal (image-point cloud) alignment makes visual features keep modality-shared (redundant) information like depth and discard modality-exclusive information like color and texture; cross-view alignment keeps more texture.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-modal contrastive alignment biases learned representations toward information shared across modalities and discards modality-specific information.

record.problems: The authors note that pretraining and finetuning results are subject to stochastic effects. The representation-content assessment covers selected characteristics such as color, texture, and depth; the text does not report uncertainty estimates for these findings.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were recorded as rows because the reported downstream performance metrics and supplementary proxy-depth-loss comparisons do not measure any listed claim version or inter-model representation similarity.

untested.parts: No scale/capability sweep and no similarity measure between independently trained models.
Modalities are images and 3D point clouds, alignment is trained in by the GEO loss; no image-caption alignment versus model quality.
No seed comparisons or shared-feature/subspace analysis.
No mapping, stitching, or relative-representation tests between models; the linear layer is internal to one model.
No recurring interpretable features or circuits across models.
No similarity metrics or settings compared.
No measurement of incomplete or plateauing inter-model alignment or its causes.

record.verdict_notes: Tangentially relevant to V7's idea that shared training objectives shape what representations encode, but the study measures information content of single models, not convergence between models, so no verdict is given.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep over model size or capability and no measure of similarity between independently trained models.
The cross-modal pairing is images and 3D point clouds, not images and captions; no alignment trend with model quality is measured.
No comparison of seeds, shared features, or shared subspaces across independently trained networks.
The linear layer separates loss feature spaces; the study does not test mapping representations between models, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired mapping.
No recurring interpretable features or circuits are identified across models.
No representation-similarity metric, metric setting, or input-distribution dependence is compared.
The study does not test whether inter-model alignment is incomplete or plateaus, or whether shared training data or objectives explain convergence.

rows.subject: VIEW
rows.stage_stated: Self-supervised pretraining on ScanNet for 5 epochs after supervised ImageNet initialization
rows.operation_detail: Pretraining with the cross-view VIEW contrastive loss
rows.measure: Texture information retained in visual representations
rows.note: This is a finding about retained visual content, not similarity between independently trained models.
rows.check: Measures texture retention under a training loss, not inter-model representational similarity; correctly unlinked.

rows.subject: GEO
rows.stage_stated: Self-supervised pretraining on ScanNet for 5 epochs after supervised ImageNet initialization
rows.operation_detail: Pretraining with the cross-modal GEO contrastive loss
rows.measure: Depth information retained in visual representations
rows.note: The paper describes depth as redundant information shared across the image and point-cloud modalities.
rows.check: Depth retention under an imposed cross-modal loss; alignment is induced by the objective, not measured as emergent convergence.

rows.subject: VIEW+GEO
rows.stage_stated: Self-supervised pretraining on ScanNet for 5 epochs after supervised ImageNet initialization
rows.operation_detail: Pretraining with VIEW and GEO losses on the same visual features
rows.measure: Retention of complementary and redundant visual information
rows.value: The combination does not make complementary information from the two losses complement one another; the shared feature space loses complementary information and less accentuates redundant details.
rows.note: This reports the effect of jointly aligning features, not convergence among independently trained models.
rows.check: Effect of jointly aligning losses on retained information; not a claim-version measure.

rows.subject: VIEW+GEO (lin)
rows.stage_stated: Self-supervised pretraining on ScanNet for 5 epochs after supervised ImageNet initialization
rows.operation_detail: Pretraining with VIEW and GEO losses separated by a linear layer

conditions.value: linear layer separates VIEW and GEO feature spaces

rows.measure: Retention of complementary and redundant visual information
rows.baseline: VIEW+GEO with directly aligned feature spaces
rows.value: Lifting direct alignment improves the combined model on all three frozen downstream tasks and allows it to preserve more complementary information.
rows.note: The three tasks are depth prediction, image reconstruction, and semantic segmentation.
rows.check: Value is a downstream frozen-task comparison (study's own method variants, >10% improvement on all three tasks); not convergence.

rows.subject: All four Pri3D variations (aggregate)
rows.stage_stated: Self-supervised pretraining on ScanNet for 5 epochs after supervised ImageNet initialization
rows.operation_detail: Assessing color information through frozen downstream representations
rows.measure: Color information retained in visual representations
rows.value: All model variations discard most of the color information.
rows.note: The paper states this as an aggregate finding across the four variations.
rows.check: Qualitative color-loss observation across variants; unrelated to inter-model similarity.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
